chapter: Queens Terrace, Decca records and Amen
title: The gap in recording and Mayo Williams
summary: Why 18 months passed between sessions; Mayo Williams signed the band and got composer credit.

story.theme_name: Getting paid for records: royalties, publishing and flat fees
story.community_name: Royalties, publishing and who owns the song

blocks.x: We got to the Queens Terrace, we got to the Horseshoe Bar in Sunnyside and did we go anyplace else after that?
Why is there such a long gap, for example, between March 11, 1940 to October 21, 1941; that's eighteen months. How come it took so long to make another record?
Mayo Williams was the one who signed the band?
So obviously Mayo's got his name on "I'm Just a Substitute for Love"; did he get his name on "The Man with the Funny Horn" too?
He didn't put his name on that one.
"Substitute for Love"; he's got it on that?
Yeah, I know that. So that's why you're having trouble with getting the--
